missed-opportunity.title: Pia’s recovery after a missed filing action
missed-opportunity.summary: A missed action leads to a factual opportunity check and the next feasible attempt.

nodes.label: Filing did not happen
nodes.description: Record the missed action without erasing earlier useful practice.

nodes.label: Desk opportunity existed?
nodes.description: Pia was at a family appointment; distinguish an absent opportunity from a missed cue.

nodes.label: Record unavailable opportunity
nodes.description: For the appointment day, note the context rather than calling it a failed available attempt.

nodes.label: Inspect cue or setup
nodes.description: If a desk opportunity did exist, check whether the cue was noticed and materials were available.

nodes.label: Resume at next feasible cue
nodes.description: Use the normal modest action; add an alternate cue only if recurring context changes warrant it.

evidence-review.title: Wen’s maintenance decision
evidence-review.summary: Separate useful observations from causal claims, then choose the next version of the routine.

nodes.label: Read two-week bag-packing log
nodes.description: The record includes fewer searches, two unavailable evenings and one missed cue.

nodes.label: Still useful and feasible?
nodes.description: Compare search benefit, setup effort and the current timetable.

nodes.label: Keep normal cue
nodes.description: Keep after-dinner packing when the benefit and fit remain worthwhile.

nodes.label: Change or retire deliberately
nodes.description: If the purpose or context has changed, simplify the setup, choose another cue or stop an unnecessary routine.

nodes.label: Set next review and recovery
nodes.description: Record a late-shift branch and a review date; a lighter timetable remains an alternate explanation for improvement.
